items.title: Partition and quadrature bounds for a periodic PIC shape

references.title: R. W. Hockney and J. W. Eastwood, Computer Simulation Using Particles, Sections 2-2-3 and 5-2
A. Myers, P. Colella, and B. Van Straalen, A 4th-Order Particle-in-Cell Method with Phase-Space Remapping for the Vlasov–Poisson Equation, Section 2

items.statement:
Let $d,L,N,h,\eta_\varepsilon,Z_{\varepsilon,h}$, and $w_j^{\varepsilon,h}$ have the meanings in [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]] and [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]]. For a finite signed Borel measure $\mu$ on the torus, write $\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}=|\mu|(\mathbb T_L^d)$ and define
$$ (P_h^\varepsilon\mu)_j=h^{-d}\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)\,d\mu(x). $$ Put $$ C_\eta=\frac{L^d}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_{aa}\eta_\varepsilon\|_\infty,\qquad Z_{\min}=L^d\min_{x\in\mathbb T_L^d}\eta_\varepsilon(x)>0 . $$ Then $\sum_jw_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)=1$ for every $x$, and $Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)\ge Z_{\min}$. The measure assignment satisfies $$ \left|(P_h^\varepsilon\mu)_j-(\eta_\varepsilon*\mu)(x_j)\right| \le \frac{C_\eta\|\eta_\varepsilon\|_\infty}{Z_{\min}}\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}h^2 . $$ For $g\in C^2(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^m)$ with finite $m\ge1$ (including scalar $m=1$), use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ and $\|g\|_\infty=\sup_y|g(y)|_2$. Define the translation-uniform constant
$$ C_{\eta,g}=\frac{L^d}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d \sup_{x,y\in\mathbb T_L^d}\left|\partial_{y_a y_a}\bigl[\eta_\varepsilon(y-x)g(y)\bigr]\right|_2 . $$ The gathered nodal samples satisfy the explicit bound $$ \left|\sum_jw_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)g(x_j)-(\eta_\varepsilon*g)(x)\right| \le \frac{C_{\eta,g}+C_\eta\|g\|_\infty}{Z_{\min}}h^2 \qquad(x\in\mathbb T_L^d). $$

items.title: Fixed-regularization periodic PIC force consistency on a smooth density

references.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 5, Finite Difference Approximation
A. Myers, P. Colella, and B. Van Straalen, A 4th-Order Particle-in-Cell Method with Phase-Space Remapping for the Vlasov–Poisson Equation, Sections 2.1–2.2
R. W. Hockney and J. W. Eastwood, Computer Simulation Using Particles, Section 5-4

items.statement:
Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and a finite signed Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb T_L^d$ with total mass $Q$. Let $\rho_\varepsilon=\eta_\varepsilon*\mu-Q/L^d$ and let $\phi_\varepsilon$ be its unique zero-mean periodic Poisson potential from [[thm-periodic-pic-continuum-regularized-poisson-kernel-is-smooth]]. Put $E_\varepsilon=-\nabla\phi_\varepsilon$. Use the shape and periodic centered-difference Poisson operator of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]] and [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]]. Let $s_h=P_h^\varepsilon\mu-Q/L^d$, let $A_h\phi_h=s_h$ with $\bar\phi_h=0$, set $E_{h,j}=-D^0\phi_h$, and gather $G_hE_h$ using the same shape. Define
$$ C_{\rm dep}=\frac{C_\eta\|\eta_\varepsilon\|_\infty}{Z_{\min}}\|\mu\|_{\rm TV},\quad C_{\rm FD}=\frac1{12}\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_a^4\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty,\quad C_{\rm src}=C_{\rm dep}+C_{\rm FD}, $$ where $C_\eta,Z_{\min}$ are from [[lem-periodic-pic-shape-partition-and-quadrature-bound]]. Put $$ C_3=\frac16\left(\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_a^3\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad C_{\rm int}=\frac{C_{\eta,E}+\|E_\varepsilon\|_\infty C_\eta}{Z_{\min}}, \quad C_{\eta,E}=\frac{L^d}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d \sup_{x,y\in\mathbb T_L^d}\left|\partial_{y_a y_a}[\eta_\varepsilon(y-x)E_\varepsilon(y)]\right|_2 . $$ For vector fields, $\|V\|_\infty=\sup_x|V(x)|_2$ (the maximum of Euclidean lengths for grid fields); the derivatives in $C_{\eta,E}$ use this same Euclidean norm. Then the source $s_h$ is compatible and $$ \|G_hE_h-\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon\|_\infty \le L^{d/2}h^{2-d/2}\left(\gamma_{N,L}C_{\rm src}+C_3\right) +C_{\rm int}h^2. $$
The displayed $\gamma_{N,L}$ is the actual finite-grid inverse/derivative norm of [[thm-periodic-pic-poisson-residual-to-gathered-force-bound]] and satisfies $\gamma_{N,L}\le L/4$. Thus for $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ this fixed-$\varepsilon$ force error tends to zero as $h\to0$. Every constant depends on the stated smooth regularized solution and kernel; this is not an $\varepsilon\to0$ estimate.

items.title: Fourth-order RK4 trajectory error for the fixed-grid periodic PIC ODE

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.330, Introduction to Numerical Analysis, Chapter 5
R. W. Hockney and J. W. Eastwood, Computer Simulation Using Particles, Chapter 4

items.statement:
Fix $\varepsilon>0$, grid width $h$, particle count $P\ge1$, and final time $T>0$. Apply classical RK4 from [[alg-periodic-pic-classical-rk4-step]] to the autonomous finite-dimensional PIC system
$$ \dot Z=F_{\varepsilon,h}(Z),\qquad (F_{\varepsilon,h}(Z))_p=\frac1P\sum_{r=1}^P \mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z_p,z_r),\qquad z_p=(X_p,V_p). $$ Let $Z(t)$ be an exact solution on $[0,T]$. Assume $F_{\varepsilon,h}$ is $C^4$ on an open set containing a common compact convex tube $\mathcal T$; the exact path, all numerical states, and every RK4 stage generated from both the exact and numerical starting states lie in $\mathcal T$; and all derivatives of $F_{\varepsilon,h}$ through order four are bounded there. Choose a uniform step $0<h_t\le h_0$ with $h_0>0$, initialize exactly, and retain every time $t_k=kh_t\le T$ for integers $k\ge0$; $T/h_t$ need not be an integer. The stage hypotheses concern each step ending by $T$. Put $$ L_F=2L_{\varepsilon,h},\qquad L_*=L_Fe^{L_Fh_0}, $$ and choose $C_4$ so that the exact-start defect on this tube is at most $C_4s^5$ for admitted steps $0<s\le h_0$ ending by $T$. The local-order supplier gives such constants for a sufficiently small positive $h_0$ under the stated smoothness and tube assumptions. Then, for every grid time $t_k=kh_t\le T$, $$ \|Z_k-Z(t_k)\|_2\le \begin{cases} C_4\dfrac{e^{L_*T}-1}{L_*}h_t^4,&L_*>0,\\[4pt] C_4Th_t^4,&L_*=0. \end{cases} $$
The tube, exact-solution, and stage-admissibility hypotheses are conditional; this is a fixed-$\varepsilon$, fixed-grid finite-particle time error, not a continuum or singular-force estimate.

references.title: R. W. Hockney and J. W. Eastwood, Computer Simulation Using Particles, Chapters 4 and 5
A. Myers, P. Colella, and B. Van Straalen, A 4th-Order Particle-in-Cell Method with Phase-Space Remapping for the Vlasov–Poisson Equation, Section 2

items.statement:
Fix $\varepsilon>0$, grid width $h$, particle count $P\ge1$, and $T>0$. Use uniform RK4 times $t_n=n\Delta t$ for integers $n\ge0$, with $0<\Delta t\le h_0$, where $h_0$ is the positive admitted step-width bound in the RK4 tube/defect hypotheses below. Retain all $t_n\le T$; no integer value of $T/\Delta t$ is required. Assume the smooth fixed-regularization hypotheses of [[thm-periodic-pic-smooth-density-grid-force-consistency]], and that the translated unit-source regularized densities $\eta_\varepsilon(\cdot-y)-L^{-d}$ satisfy its derivative bounds uniformly in $y$. Let $\delta_{\varepsilon,h}$ be the uniform phase-kernel defect from [[thm-periodic-pic-mean-field-error-with-force-defect]]. The consistency theorem gives the explicit estimate
$$ \delta_{\varepsilon,h} \le |cQ|\left[ L^{d/2}h^{2-d/2} igl(\gamma_{N,L}C_{m src}^{(1)}+C_3^{(1)} igr) +C_{m int}^{(1)}h^2 ight], $$ where $C_{m src}^{(1)},C_3^{(1)},C_{m int}^{(1)}$ are the constants of that theorem evaluated at a unit point source; translation of the continuum source leaves their derivative suprema unchanged, while the shape quadrature constants are independent of the translate. Define the RK4 empirical measure by $
u_{P,h}^{\Delta t}(t_n)=P^{-1}\sum_{p=1}^P\delta_{z_p^{\Delta t}(t_n)}$. Put $$ \delta_0=W_1(
u_0^h,\mu_0),\qquad C_{m RK}=  egin{cases} C_4(e^{L_*T}-1)/L_*,&L_*>0,\ C_4T,&L_*=0, \end{cases} $$ using the constants of [[thm-periodic-pic-rk4-finite-time-error-on-a-controlled-tube]]. For exact initialization, a common admissible initial coupling, and the same compact-tube hypotheses, the RK4 empirical measure $
u_{P,h}^{\Delta t}(t_n)$ and regularized characteristic solution $\mu_\varepsilon(t_n)$ satisfy $$ W_1\!\left(
u_{P,h}^{\Delta t}(t_n),\mu_\varepsilon(t_n)ight) \le  rac{C_{m RK}}{\sqrt P}\Delta t^4 +e^{2L_\varepsilon T}\left(\delta_0+T\delta_{\varepsilon,h}ight), \qquad t_n\le T. $$
The terms are time error, prescribed initial empirical error, and fixed-$\varepsilon$ mesh-force error. No universal rate for $\delta_0$ and no $\varepsilon	o0$ singular Vlasov–Poisson limit is asserted.
